clue.text: Hilarious beyond value?

definitions.meaning: something wildly funny is said, colloquially, to be beyond price
worth so much that no sum could buy it

explanation.surface: A question about whether something terribly funny is also too precious to put a price on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: colloquially very amusing, and literally too valuable to be priced.

clue.text: Just beat time in the end for small flute

parts.note: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly, just edging ahead

indicators.note: the end of the word time supplies its closing letter only

explanation.surface: A musician narrowly wins a race against the clock, rewarded with a little flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, essentially a small flute blown at one end.

clue.text: Beg one extra having scoffed half of plum

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so the outer letters swallow the other piece

parts.note: more means additional or extra

indicators.note: taking half of the word plum leaves its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for one more helping after gobbling half a plum.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beseech or plead earnestly, a direct synonym for begging.

clue.text: Fish tails in the rice bowl

indicators.note: the tails of words are their final letters, taken from each of the three words listed

explanation.surface: Fish tails are served up in a bowl of rice.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snakelike fish, a crossword staple.

clue.text: Profitable job student hasn't started

indicators.note: the word for the student loses its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is someone studying, a student

explanation.surface: A student is lamenting not having begun a lucrative job.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner, as in a nice little earner, is an enterprise or job that brings in money.

clue.text: Poor dope with strep, bunged up

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorry fool with a strep throat is congested.
explanation.walkthrough: Strep is short for a streptococcal throat infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stoppered has had a plug or bung put in it, so it is sealed shut.

clue.text: Expression of contempt when son leaves party

indicators.note: the son departs, so his letter is removed from the party word

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone snorts in disdain as their son walks out of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is an exclamation of scorn or dismissal, a way of saying humbug.

clue.text: Keep playing cricket? Give it a twirl!

definitions.meaning: to carry on batting at the crease
a majorette's stick spun in the air

explanation.surface: A cheerful urging to stay in the game, then spin something round.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BAT ON for the cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorettes twirl a stick in parades; batting on means continuing to bat in cricket.

clue.text: Hospital overlooking a peculiar African city

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that overlooks another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
rare means unusual or peculiar

explanation.surface: A hospital looks out over a strange city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe, a city in southern Africa.

clue.text: Backing up, very cold outside and in

indicators.note: the cold word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: polar regions are icy, so polar means extremely cold

indicators.note: backing sends the word up in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone backs up in the freezing weather, both outdoors and indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside and in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be fashionable and well liked, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Remote route redirected

indicators.note: sending something a different way suggests these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters also run on into the next word, but that is a coincidence: the anagram signal reworks this word alone

explanation.surface: A distant road has been rerouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means farther from the centre, so distant or remote, as in outer suburbs.

clue.text: Bravery, key perhaps, in possession of drinker?

parts.note: in British slang bottle means nerve or courage
a key is one example of something that opens

explanation.surface: Courage and a key are what a drinker carries around.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle for courage is British slang, as in losing your bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinker might well carry a tool for removing caps, hence the question mark on this cryptic hint.

clue.text: Jack, boy in weatherproof material

parts.note: a jack tar, or simply tar or jack, is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy called Jack wrapped in waterproof cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is heavy waterproofed canvas, used to cover things against rain.

clue.text: Carry enormous animal

definitions.meaning: to support or transport a load
the grizzly is an example of a huge beast

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to carry and the name of a large furry mammal.

clue.text: People are competitive

definitions.meaning: a group of people sharing descent, an ethnic group
a plural verb: they compete for speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an ethnic group of people and a verb meaning to contend in speed.

clue.text: Pacy solo almost fluffed in Caribbean ballad

indicators.note: to fluff is to bungle, so these letters are jumbled
almost the whole word solo, leaving off its last letter

explanation.surface: A fast-paced solo is botched during a Caribbean song.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a Trinidadian song style, often topical, which counts as a Caribbean ballad.

clue.text: A rise in addition

parts.note: a swell is a rise, as of the sea or of sound

explanation.surface: A bare note of an increase, plus something more.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or too, adding something further.

clue.text: Two cats beat it!

indicators.note: two cats asks for the word for a male cat twice

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An exclamation telling two cats to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' looks like scram, but it means a thing to be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a drum played by hand, so it is the thing you beat.

clue.text: Dallas diva or wayward Catalan artist…

indicators.note: wayward means wandering off course, so these letters go astray

explanation.surface: A diva from Dallas or a headstrong painter from Catalonia.
explanation.definitionFit: This surrealist painter was born in Figueres in Catalonia, Spain.

clue.text: Audible programme for composer

indicators.note: audible signals the word for programme as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a programme is a list of items or events

explanation.surface: A programme you can hear, made for a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Month up and exhausted initially, give up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word exhausted

explanation.surface: Late in the year and worn out, someone quits.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield, giving up territory or rights.

clue.text: …his stand comfort and love primarily?

parts.note: ease means comfort or relief

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of love

explanation.surface: Following on from the artist: what his stand offers is comfort and love.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 17 Across, so 'his' refers to the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holds the canvas while working, so it is that artist's stand.

clue.text: Pirates disturbed trail

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Pirates disturbed a path they were following.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge or trail wearily along.

clue.text: Cap removed from white drink

indicators.note: the cap is the top letter of the word, taken off

parts.note: pale means whitish, lacking colour

explanation.surface: Someone pops the top off a white drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a kind of beer, so a drink.

clue.text: Lease back half of Swiss property?

indicators.note: the back half of the word keeps only its last three letters

parts.note: a chalet is a typical Alpine house, as in Switzerland

explanation.surface: Renting out the rear half of a house in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: To let is to rent out property, the same as leasing it.

clue.text: Hit me

definitions.meaning: a song at the top of the charts
oneself, as in looking after yourself first

explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topper is called this, and so is oneself in the idiom of looking after yourself.
